version.description: Schema version of this file; currently 1.

name.description: Team slug: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter.

product.description: Name of the product the team builds.

humans.description: Trusted humans. Optional; when omitted, trusted humans are repo writers and full chat-workspace members.

name.description: Display name of the trusted human.

tracker.description: Username or id in the issue tracker.

chat.description: Username or id in the chat workspace.

identities.description: How this human is known on each connected system; at least one is required.

version.description: Exact catalog release this team uses, for example "1.0.0"; must match the catalog in the agent images.

path.description: Directory of ejected catalog files, relative to this file.

catalog.description: Which catalog of roles and skills the team uses.

name.description: Short name used to refer to this repository in grants.

url.description: Repository location: host/owner/repo, an https URL or a git@ address.

kind.description: Role of the repository: primary (the product, at most one), baseline, infra or other.

checks.description: Commands an agent runs before pushing, covering only what a change affects (for example lint and the tests related to changed files). CI runs the full suite. When omitted, agents work out the affected checks themselves.

conventions.description: How work is done in this repository, as free text: commits, branches, pull request title and body, tests. For repositories whose own files (CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, the pull request template) cannot say it. Agents read it in addition to those files.

ticket_link.description: Extra ways this repository's pull request body names its ticket, as regular expressions with one {key} placeholder for the ticket key (for example `Ticket: {key}`). A pull request is always linked by the ticket key in its branch name, its title, or a closing keyword in its body (`Closes ACME-12`); these patterns add to the last. A key mentioned in the body in any other way links nothing.

instructions.description: Extra files in this repository that agents read before they work, relative to its root, for example ["CLAUDE.md"]. A project CLAUDE.md is not loaded into agent sessions unless it is listed here.

items.description: A repository the team works in.

repos.description: Repositories the team works in; at least one.

handle.description: Unique lowercase handle; used as the agent's hostname label and mention name.

pronouns.description: Pronouns shown in the agent's profile.

role.description: Catalog role this agent plays, for example "developer".

extends.description: Extra catalog roles or skill bundles layered on top of the role.

model.description: LLM model for this agent; the runtime adapter's default when omitted.

identities.description: How this agent is known on each connected system. The office recognizes the agent's own activity only by an exact match with these.

vcs.description: Login of this agent on the VCS host, for example "acme-sam[bot]".

tracker.description: Username or id of this agent in the issue tracker.

chat.description: Username or id of this agent in the chat workspace.

repos.description: Repository access by repo name, "kind:<primary|baseline|infra|other>" or "*"; values are "read" or "write".

tools.description: Tools for this agent only; they replace team-level tools of the same name.

version.description: Exact version to install, for example "1.23.4".

source.description: Where mise gets the tool, as a mise backend and name such as ubi:vendor/their-cli or npm:their-cli. Defaults to the tool name, which mise looks up in its registry.

anyOf.description: Subcommand verbs the agent may run.

program.description: Optional; when given it must be the tool's own name.

args.description: Every condition must hold for the rule to apply.

present.description: Whether one of the flags must (true) or must not (false) be present.

names.description: Flag spellings whose value is checked.

match.description: Whether the flag value is in or not in `values`.

index.description: Position after the subcommand words, from 0.

pattern.description: Case-insensitive regular expression the argument matches.

items.description: A condition on the command arguments.

reason.description: Why the rule exists; shown when it decides a call.

allow.description: What the agent may run: "all" (any arguments), a list of first subcommands, or structured rules. Installing a tool allows nothing by itself. The built-in denies still win.

url.description: Image URL to use as the avatar.

items.description: An AI agent on the team.

people.description: The agents on the team; may be empty.

poll_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between polls when events is "poll".

poll_warn_after_minutes.description: Minutes without a successful poll of an event source before the office logs a warning. Default 10.

channel.description: Team chat channel where the office mirrors agent-to-agent questions and answers, so humans can follow them. Without it they go to the ticket of the asking work item, or only to its journal.

statuses.description: Maps canonical statuses to the status names used in your tracker.

rules.description: Rules added to the preset. A rule with a preset rule's id replaces it; { id, disabled: true } removes it.

id.description: Unique id. A rule with the same id as a preset rule replaces it.

on.description: Event type or types that trigger the rule.

anyOf.description: Move the ticket to a canonical status.
Assign the ticket.
Post a rendered template as a comment (on the ticket by default).
Schedule a work item for an agent.
Send a rendered template to a person or channel.

disabled.description: Set to true to remove the rule.

anyOf.description: A workflow rule.
Removes the preset rule with this id.

templates.description: Comment and notification templates by id, with {{variable}} placeholders. They override built-in templates with the same id.

needs_human_label.description: Ticket label that keeps work with a human. Default "needs-human".

workflow.description: How work moves through the team.

agent_loop_guard.description: Stops agents from triggering each other in endless loops. Limits only runs triggered by agents or automation; humans are never limited.

max_runs_per_item_per_hour.description: Maximum runs per work item per hour triggered by agents or automation; humans are never limited.

usage.description: Thresholds that slow down work as the LLM usage limit approaches.

defer_scheduled_at.description: Fraction of the usage limit at which scheduled work is deferred.

pause_automatic_at.description: Fraction of the usage limit at which all automatic work pauses.

shared.description: Groups of people who use one LLM subscription, as lists of handles. A usage report from any member applies to all of them.

acknowledge.description: The reactions that show people their message or comment was picked up.

chat.description: React with eyes to a chat message from a trusted person when the agent has seen it. Default on.

vcs.description: React with eyes to each pull request comment the agent is about to answer, when its round starts. Needs a vcs adapter with vcs.reactions. Default on.

feedback.description: How agents act on feedback from trusted people beyond the first round.

follow_up_round.description: Start another round when feedback arrived after the agent was offered its work. Default on.

merged_prs.description: Schedule the author to answer feedback on a merged pull request. Switches the preset rule merged-feedback-follow-up. Default on.

doc_comments.description: Schedule the author of a knowledge document to answer a trusted person's comments on it. Switches the preset rule doc-feedback-to-author. Default on.

ticket_comments.description: Start a round for the assigned agent when a trusted person comments on its ticket, and send a handed-back ticket back to its last worker. Switches the preset rules ticket-comment-to-assignee and ticket-comment-reactivates-ticket. Default on.

hand_back.description: What happens to a ticket when an agent hands its work back.

reassign.description: Who an agent's hand-back assigns the ticket to: the requester, or none to leave the assignee alone (the ticket still moves: to review when done, to blocked when blocked). Edits the preset rules hand-back-to-requester and hand-back-blocked-to-requester. Default requester.

fallback.description: Who stands in when a ticket has no known requester: the first human in humans, or none to skip. Default first_human.

tickets.description: How tickets and pull requests relate.

prs_per_ticket.description: How many pull requests a ticket may have. one: ost pr open refuses a second one for a ticket and the ticket moves to done when its pull request merges; many: several are allowed and the ticket moves to done when the agent hands its work back as done and every pull request linked to it is closed with at least one merged. Edits the preset rules pr-merged-done, pr-closed-ready, hand-back-to-requester and second-pr-comment. Default one.

follow_up.description: Send a pull request that starts to conflict with its base, for example after another one merged, back to its agent author to rebase. Switches the preset rule conflict-back-to-author. Default on.

retry.description: How a failing work item is retried: exponential backoff, then blocked; and whether a human's signal brings a blocked item back.

on_signal.description: Retry a blocked work item when a trusted human moves its ticket, assigns it, reviews or comments on its pull request, or replies in its chat thread. Default on.

base_minutes.description: Wait after the first failed run of a work item; doubles with each failure.

cap_minutes.description: Longest wait between two attempts at a failing work item.

max_failures.description: Consecutive failed runs after which the work item is blocked and its requester told.

merge.description: Merging an agent's pull request when an allowed approver approves it (opt-in).

on_approval.description: Let an agent merge its own pull request, with ost pr merge, when an allowed approver approves it. Off by default: without it the verb refuses and nothing is scheduled. Adds the preset rules approved-merge and approved-merge-after-feedback. Needs a vcs adapter with vcs.merge. It never bypasses branch protection or rulesets; the code host stays the final gate.

approvers.description: Who may approve a merge: humans (the people in humans, or anyone with write access when humans is omitted), human:<id> (one human, by vcs identity), role:<role> (the agent playing a catalog role) or a handle (an agent, or a human by vcs login). Default humans.

method.description: How the pull request is merged: queue (the host's merge queue), merge or squash. When omitted, outstaff uses what the repository has: its merge queue, else a method its settings allow.

repos.description: Names of the repos (from repos) whose pull requests may be merged this way. Default: every repo an agent can write to.

max_lines.description: Guidance for agents: keep chat replies to about this many lines. It is a hard limit only for the office's own automatic notices (status lines, run notifications). An agent's reply is never cut; one over a high safety cap is split into several messages.

always_link.description: Link tickets, pull requests and documents instead of mentioning bare ids.

omit.description: Details left out of chat messages.

canvas.description: Let roles that declare the design.canvas capability use Claude's Artifact tools (the Design canvas). Needs the claude-agent-sdk runtime signed in with a Claude account. Default on; it does nothing for a role without the capability.

chat.description: How agents take chat messages, and what they show in chat.

parallel_sessions.description: How many chat sessions an agent runs at once, beside its active work item. A message beyond that waits for a free session.

profile.description: Publish the agent's profile in chat: role, status, and current work grouped by ticket or pull request. Needs a chat adapter with chat.agentProfile. Default on.

The condition must not hold.
The linked ticket is in one of these canonical statuses.
A ticket.moved event moved the ticket into one of these statuses.
Who caused the event.
Who the ticket is assigned to.
The ticket has this label. "$needs_human" means the configured needs-human label.
Who authored the pull request.
The actor of the event is (or is not) an allowed approver of a merge, as policies.merge.approvers says.
The pull request is (or is not) a draft.
The pull request is (or is not) open.
The pull request is (or is not) merged.
The review or comment in the event has (or lacks) text: a non-blank body, or for a review, inline comments.
The review state in the event, for example "approved".
An agent.handed_back event carries one of these statuses: done, waiting or blocked.
An agent.handed_back event is for a work item of one of these kinds, for example "review_feedback".
An allowed approver (policies.merge.approvers) has approved the pull request and none has requested changes since (or, with false, that does not hold).
Every pull request linked to the ticket is closed and at least one of them is merged (or, with false, that does not hold).
At least one pull request linked to the ticket is still open (or, with false, none is).
The ticket has two or more pull requests that are open or merged (or, with false, fewer). Closed ones that were never merged do not count.
The agent's latest work on the ticket ended with a hand-back as done (or, with false, did not).
